introduction.definition: A chemical preparation (make-down) tank makes solutions such as polymer, lime milk or coagulant from dry powder and water. A screw feeder doses powder in proportion to the dilution water, an agitator wets and dissolves it, and the solution is held for ageing before the dosing pumps take it.
applications: Polymer make-down for clarifiers and sludge dewatering
Lime, soda ash and coagulant preparation

pressure.title: Make-down: wetting, dissolving, ageing
pressure.description: Dry chemicals must be wetted evenly and dissolved without lumps ("fish-eyes" with polymer). The feeder doses powder in proportion to the dilution water to reach the target strength (polymer often ~ 0.1–0.5 %, lime milk ~ 5–10 %). Polymer solutions need gentle mixing and ageing time (~ 30–60 min) to fully uncoil before use.

foundation: Level concrete plinth; anchor the skid; bund or drain for chemical / oil spills.
alignment: Skid level; check pump–motor alignment where not close-coupled; supports so piping loads do not reach equipment nozzles.
piping: Isolation valves and bypass for maintenance; drains and vents; correct materials for the chemical; label lines and flow direction.
commissioning: Pressure-test piping; flush; check rotation and interlocks; calibrate instruments; run on water before chemicals.

routine.task: Check hopper level and feeder calibration.

lubrication: Motor and drive bearings greased / oiled to maker schedule; gearbox oil changed by hours or oil analysis.

safety: Dust: extraction and masks; polymer spills are very slippery; lime is caustic.

script.narration: This module introduces the Chemical Preparation Tank.
A chemical preparation (make-down) tank makes solutions such as polymer, lime milk or coagulant from dry powder and water.
A screw feeder doses powder in proportion to the dilution water, an agitator wets and dissolves it, and the solution is held for ageing before the dosing pumps take it.
Typical applications include polymer make-down for clarifiers and sludge dewatering; lime, soda ash and coagulant preparation.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Preparation Tank: Agitator Shaft & Impeller.

script.narration: How the Chemical Preparation Tank works.
Dry chemical is loaded into the hopper.
The screw feeder doses it into the tank.
Dilution water is metered in.
The agitator dissolves and ages the solution.
Solution goes to the dosing pumps.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.
Dry chemicals must be wetted evenly and dissolved without lumps ("fish-eyes" with polymer).

video_tutorials.title: Chemical Preparation Tank — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Chemical Preparation Tank.
Check hopper level and feeder calibration.
Clean tank of lumps and deposits.
Overhaul agitator gearbox.
Watch for fish-eyes / lumps: blocked dosing pumps. Common cause: poor wetting.
Watch for feeder bridging: no powder flow. Common cause: damp powder.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
